sections.title: Player-facing description
sections.body: A great arch of pale carved stone rises three wagons wide, its keystone leafed in gold and its faces worn smooth by a century of carved caravans setting out. Beneath it runs a permanent little fair: toll-counters clacking, a crier calling the morning rates, a stall hawking painted gate-charms, and the smell of fried dough and hot sealing-wax.

items: Title: Location Exploration Mechanics
Player Safe: Players can navigate, search, read customs, inspect hazards Emeris Capital Gate when it is present in the fiction.
Gm Only: Use the roll only when the player's method, stakes, and consequence are concrete.

No Roll Reveals: Surface read: A great arch of pale carved stone three wagons wide, with toll-counters clacking beneath it and the green dark of Sablewood waiting beyond. Give obvious visible facts freely; roll for meaning, risk, leverage, cost, or a hidden angle.

A flat read of Emeris Capital Gate hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear...
Fear Spends: Reveal who benefits from the current situation. Make the cost personal without closing off player agency.
Condition Options: No official condition unless a hazard creates Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable
Search Loot: The gate is a vivid starting place and route threshold, not a missing-ward reveal.

A great arch of pale carved stone three wagons wide, with toll-counters clacking beneath it and the green dark of Sablewood waiting beyond. Block2: Pale carved stone arches over three wagon lanes. A permanent gate market clings to the wall where the city becomes road. The gate sells confidence, supplies, and paperwork before the forest gets a vote. Nothing is missing from the public face of the gate; the tension is the shift from city order to road risk. Detail Fried dough, hot sealing-wax, brass polish, carriage dust, and rain waiting in the forest air. Block4: The place changes even if the PCs stand still. Local people, creatures, weather, signage, and ward behavior all keep moving around the scene. Official confidence can make road risk feel smaller than it is. Buying one more charm can become a joke or a delay. Crowds make last-minute questions public. A cheerful notice updates the road fee while nobody mentions why. A charm seller offers a discount for travelers who look doomed. Let the place be funny through overconfident signage, awkward forms, stubborn local habits, and magic that refuses corporate language.
